name: Elamites
place: the lowlands of Susa and the highlands of Anshan
desc: A people of two worlds, the hot plain of Susa and the high valleys of the Zagros, who wrote in scripts of their own, traded tin and stone from the east, and fought Sumer, Akkad and Babylon for two thousand years.
source: Excavations at Susa (from 1897), Anshan (Tal-e Malyan) and Chogha Zanbil; Linear Elamite, deciphered by François Desset and colleagues in 2022

cautious: drove the goats up to the summer pastures through the snow pass
devout: carved a snake coiled into a throne on a stone bowl
belligerent: shot a wild goat across the gorge

inventions.name: Proto-Elamite Signs
inventions.source: Proto-Elamite tablets, c. 3100–2900 BCE, from Susa to Shahr-i Sokhta: still undeciphered
inventions.desc: A script of their own, for counting grain, workers and sheep: the tribe gathers a little more lore.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and the rites and leading of others.

inventions.name: Bitumen-Compound Carving
inventions.source: Susa artisans mixed bitumen with ground stone into a paste that could be carved and polished like stone
inventions.desc: Black paste carved into lion-headed bowls and sealed jars: +2 mood, and the stores hold 10 more food.
inventions.hint: Comes from evenings at the hearth, and from working stone.

inventions.name: Glazed Bricks
inventions.source: Glazed tiles and knobs adorned the ziggurat of Chogha Zanbil (c. 1250 BCE); Susa's glazed-brick archers came later
inventions.desc: Bricks fired with a shining blue-green skin for the shrines: rites bring 10% more devotion, +2 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs pottery and fire, and builders at the kiln.

inventions.name: Highland Herding Routes
inventions.source: Herders moved between the plain of Susiana in winter and the Zagros valleys in summer, as the Bakhtiari still do
inventions.desc: Paths that follow the grass up the mountains and down again: everyone walks 5% faster, and hunting is 10% faster.
inventions.hint: Comes from scouting, and from hunting in the hills.

foods.name: Goat Cheese
foods.source: Goats were domesticated in the Zagros around 8000 BCE (Ganj Dareh)
foods.desc: Milk soured and pressed into cheese that keeps: hunger grows 8% slower, food spoils 5% slower.

foods.name: Roasted Pistachios
foods.desc: Nuts roasted over the fire and stored for winter: +2 mood, food spoils 8% slower.

finds.name: Wild Pistachio Trees
finds.desc: Hardy little trees of the Zagros slopes, heavy with nuts in autumn.

finds.name: Chlorite Stone
finds.source: Carved chlorite vessels of the 'intercultural style' from Jiroft and Tepe Yahya were traded from the Indus to Sumer
finds.desc: Soft green-black stone that carves like wood: each load is lore.

people.name: Shilhina
people.desc: She knows every pass between the plain and the high pastures.
memory: led the flocks through the pass the winter it closed early

people.name: Kutirru
people.desc: His hands turn pitch and stone into lions.
memory: carved a lion-headed bowl for the shrine of Inshushinak

people.name: Puzur-Inshushinak
people.source: Bilingual inscriptions in Akkadian and Linear Elamite, c. 2100 BCE (Louvre)
people.desc: The king who freed Elam from Akkad and wrote in Linear Elamite, the script that helped crack it four thousand years later.

people.name: Hita
people.source: The 'Treaty of Naram-Sin', c. 2250 BCE, the oldest known text in the Elamite language
people.desc: A king of Awan who made a treaty with Akkad: 'The enemy of Naram-Sin is my enemy, the friend of Naram-Sin is my friend.'

people.name: Golden-Eye
people.source: A woman buried at Shahr-i Sokhta, c. 2900–2800 BCE, wore an artificial eyeball of bitumen paste with gold lines
people.text: a tall woman from the far eastern city by the lake, with one eye that shines gold.
memory: crossed the great salt desert with a caravan of tin
people.desc: A woman of Shahr-i Sokhta, buried with the oldest known artificial eye; her name is lost, so the game names her.

people.name: Untash-Napirisha
people.label: Untash-Napirisha, Builder of the Ziggurat
people.desc: He raises a holy city in a single reign. Crafting 8, Lore 4.

people.name: Shutruk-Nahhunte
people.label: Shutruk-Nahhunte the Plunderer
people.desc: He carries the treasures of Babylon home to Susa. Combat 8.

people.name: Napir-Asu
people.label: Napir-Asu, the Bronze Queen
people.desc: A queen whose life-size bronze statue weighs as much as two oxen. Lore 6, Crafting 5.

events.title: Plain or Mountain
events.text: The plain bakes in the summer heat and the grass is gone. The herders want to drive the flocks up to the cool valleys, as their fathers did. Others want to stay by the fields.

options.label: Go up to the mountains
options.result: The flocks climb into the green valleys. The children come back brown and strong.

options.label: Stay by the fields
options.result: The people dig deeper wells and wait out the heat.

events.title: Your Enemy Is My Enemy
events.source: The treaty between Naram-Sin of Akkad and a king of Awan, sworn before Elamite and Akkadian gods
events.text: An envoy comes from the great king of the lowlands. He offers an oath: his friends will be our friends and his enemies our enemies.

options.label: Swear the oath
options.result: Gifts are exchanged and the oath is written in two tongues.

options.label: We bow to no one
options.result: The envoy leaves without a word. The young warriors cheer.

events.title: A Trophy from the Enemy
events.source: Shutruk-Nahhunte carried the stele of Naram-Sin and the Code of Hammurabi to Susa, where they were found in 1898–1901
events.text: The war party comes back with a great carved stone from an enemy town, covered in the boasts of their old king.

options.label: Set it up before our god
options.result: Under the old king's boasts, a new line is carved: it was brought here by us.

options.label: Send it back as a gift
options.result: The stone goes home. The enemy is puzzled, and quieter.

tales.name: Inshushinak Weighs the Dead
tales.source: Akkadian-language funerary tablets from Susa, early 2nd millennium BCE
tales.text: When we die, two guides take us by the hand to the house of Inshushinak, lord of Susa. There Ishmekarab and Lagamal stand at the scales, and the god looks at what our lives weighed, and says where we shall go.

tales.name: The God on the Snake Throne
tales.source: Rock relief at Kurangun, Fars, c. 1600 BCE
tales.text: High on the cliff above the river, Napirisha sits on a great snake coiled into a throne, and from the vessel in his hands the waters of life flow out to the people kneeling below. That is why our rivers never fail.

tales.name: The Woman Who Saw with Gold
tales.source: A story made up around the Shahr-i Sokhta burial
tales.text: In the city by the eastern lake a woman lost an eye. The healers made her a new one of pitch, and drew on it a golden sun. Afterwards she could see things the rest of us cannot: which caravans would come home, and which would be lost in the salt.

tales.name: The Feast of Kiririsha
tales.source: Kiririsha, 'great lady', was the mother goddess of the Elamite coast
tales.text: Once a year the great mother Kiririsha comes up from the sea to see whether her children are fed. Wherever she finds a full table and a song, she leaves the next harvest heavier; wherever she finds a locked door, she walks on.
